changes.text: 总司令到国会交还委任状。国会在前一天把谁坐着、谁鞠躬、谁脱帽逐条写进日志。作者认为，交接的形式本身，就是交接内容的一部分。

The commander in chief came before Congress to hand back his commission. The day before, Congress wrote into its journal exactly who would sit, who would bow, and who would lift a hat. On the author's reading, the form of the handover was part of what was being handed over.
I. Wrapping Up Takes Rules Too

这时的国会人很少。同一天，日志记下一个付诸表决的问题：七个州出席的国会，是否有权接受总司令的辞职？日志留下了点名表决：在本篇所见的部分名单中，除帕特里奇投了反对外，其余议员均为赞成；其中埃勒里的反对票，日志记为应一位议员的请求改成了赞成，没有写明是哪位议员。这段摘录没有显示表决结果。22日的出席记录是马萨诸塞、罗得岛、宾夕法尼亚、特拉华、马里兰、弗吉尼亚和北卡罗来纳七个州，另有新罕布什尔和南卡罗来纳各一名议员。到了23日接见当天，国会还议决立即写信给新罕布什尔、康涅狄格、纽约、新泽西、南卡罗来纳和佐治亚六个州的行政长官，催他们的代表马上到会：国会在此开会期间，出席的从未超过七个州，其中多数只有两名代表，而批准正式和约等几件要务都需要至少九个州同意。

Congress was thin at the time. The same day, the journal records a question put to the vote: "Is it the sense of Congress that seven states in Congress Assembled are competent to receive the resignation of a Commander in Chief?" The journal kept the roll call. In the portion of the roll call cited here, every member voted ay except Partridge, who voted no; Ellery's no was recorded as "changed into ay at the request of the Member", and the journal does not say which member. This excerpt does not show the result of the vote. On the 22nd the states present were Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia and North Carolina, with one member each from New Hampshire and South Carolina. And on the day of the audience itself, the 23rd, Congress resolved to write at once to the executives of New Hampshire, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, South Carolina and Georgia, demanding the immediate attendance of their delegates: during the sitting at this place there had never been more than seven states represented, most of them by only two delegates, and the ratification of the definitive treaty, among other matters, required the assent of at least nine states.
交接会上，是让交权的人站起来逐项说明、坐着的人确认接收，还是大家围坐闲聊两句、散会后补一封邮件？如果两种都能把事办完，你会选哪一种来留下记录——你希望日后被追问“权限到底收回来没有”时，手里握着的是一张签收单，还是一段谁也说不清的记忆？

At the handover meeting, do you have the person giving up authority stand and walk through each item while the receiving side sits and confirms, or does everyone chat briefly around the table and send a follow-up email afterwards? If both get the job done, which one do you choose for the record it leaves — when someone someday asks whether those permissions were actually recovered, do you want to be holding a signed receipt sheet, or a memory no one can reconstruct?

dispositions.rationale: 导语末句原以断言口吻写出，实为作者解释。中英两版都加上了作者解释的标记：中文为“作者认为”，英文为“On the author's reading”。原句中的破折号相应改为句号，其余文字不变。
证据只涉及1783年12月的接见次序，没有关于开战所需规矩的任何记录，与开战的比较无据。标题中文改为“收场也需要规矩”，英文改为“Wrapping Up Takes Rules Too”，去掉了比较。
中文原把 the Member 译成带引号的“该议员”，容易读成回指埃勒里本人，也像是原文措辞。现改为“应一位议员的请求改成了赞成，没有写明是哪位议员”，与英文 the journal does not say which member 一致。英文字段原样重新给出，文字未改。

evidence.quote: Ellery, no changed into ay at the request of the Member

dispositions.rationale: 英文的“for two minutes”与中文的“闲聊两句”不一致。英文改为“chat briefly around the table”，与中文“闲聊两句”对应。中文字段原样重新给出，文字未改。
